record.paper_title: Results and Open Problems in Mathematical General Relativity
record.original_question: For the class of S^1-symmetric vacuum Einstein spacetimes considered in the paper, where future completeness has been proved for small initial data, does future completeness still hold for large initial data?

evidence.quote: Open problem. The given proof is valid only for small data, but the future completeness for large data is an open question which may have a positive answer.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider 3+1 dimensional vacuum Einstein spacetimes admitting a spacelike U(1) (i.e. S^1) isometry group acting on a spatial manifold of the form Σ × S^1, where Σ is a compact orientable surface of genus G > 1. After dimensional reduction along the S^1 orbits, the vacuum Einstein equations on such spacetimes can be written as a 2+1 dimensional Einstein–wave map system coupled to a scalar field and a twist potential (without assuming the polarized case in which the twist vanishes).

It is known that for sufficiently small Cauchy data on Σ × S^1 of this symmetric class, the maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum development is future causally geodesically complete in the expanding time direction.

Question: Does future causal geodesic completeness of the maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum development continue to hold for arbitrary (large) S^1-symmetric Cauchy data in this class, without any smallness assumption?
artifact.status_search_result: The small-data future completeness result for U(1)/S^1-symmetric vacuum Einstein spacetimes (with higher-genus base) is due to Choquet-Bruhat and collaborators. Reviews and recent works (e.g., on the large-data global Cauchy problem for U(1)-symmetric Einstein equations and partial results in the equivariant 2+1 Einstein–wave map reduction) indicate the large-data future completeness question remains open in the unpolarized case, although progress continues on related polarized and equivariant subcases.

status_evidence.title: Future complete Einsteinian space times with U(1) symmetry, the unpolarized case
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of future-complete solutions for U(1) symmetric Einstein spacetimes (small data, unpolarized case).
status_evidence.claim: Small-data future completeness is established; large-data case not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Reflections on the U(1) problem in general relativity
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews stability results for vacuum U(1) symmetric solutions and discusses ideas for the large-data global Cauchy problem.
status_evidence.claim: The large-data global Cauchy problem for U(1)-symmetric Einstein equations is treated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: On Curvature Propagation and 'Breakdown' of the Einstein Equations on U(1) Symmetric Spacetimes
status_evidence.snippet: Initial value problem on U(1)-symmetric spacetimes; global existence in equivariant case for large data via 2+1 Einstein–wave map reduction.
status_evidence.claim: Large-data global existence is known only in special equivariant subcases, not in general.
